title: Is it haram to date?
hook: the most-asked question: what's agreed, what's discussed, and why a feeling isn't a sin

segments.voice: Yesterday: halal, from a root of untying. Your line was most things are allowed.

It's the question a lot of young Muslims ask a search bar before they'd ever ask a parent: is it haram to date? Sometimes it comes with a name attached. Someone from chemistry class. Someone from the group chat. Sometimes it isn't really about rules at all, but about a feeling, and whether having it makes you a bad person. The answers online tend to shout. Here's the calmer version: what's agreed, what's discussed, and what isn't a sin at all.
screen: `IS IT HARAM TO DATE?` → `SOMETIMES, A NAME ATTACHED.` → `AGREED, DISCUSSED, AND NOT A SIN.`

segments.voice: Start with what nearly every Muslim scholar agrees on. Sex belongs inside marriage, nikah. The Qur'an puts it as a fence, not just a rule: “And come not near unto adultery. Lo! it is an abomination and an evil way.” Come not near. That's why many teachers also advise against being secluded alone together; a hadith in Tirmidhi says that when a man and a woman are alone, the third with them is Shaytan. Now what's discussed. Dating, the way movies use the word, usually means a private relationship, with no plan, and physical closeness. Most scholars say that's outside the lines. But getting to know someone for marriage is different, and the hadith encourage it. A companion told the Prophet ﷺ he'd proposed to a woman. Have you seen her? the Prophet asked. No. Go and look at her, he said, for that is more likely to make things last between you. That's in Tirmidhi. So how do people meet and talk? Here, communities draw the line in different places. Some families arrange introductions. Some allow conversations with a parent or chaperone nearby, or in public places. Some people use apps built for marriage. Many call it getting to know someone with intention. Your own family and teachers will have a view, and they won't all match. And the part people most need to hear: a feeling isn't a sin. Camp two met the hadith that Allah forgives what the soul whispers, as long as it isn't acted on. Liking someone is human. And Ibn Majah reports the Prophet saying: nothing has been seen like marriage, for two people who love each other.
screen: `AGREED: CLOSENESS BELONGS IN NIKAH.` · `GO AND LOOK AT HER: ENCOURAGED.` · `HOW TO MEET: FAMILIES DIFFER.` · `A FEELING ISN'T A SIN.`

segments.voice: Think of a strong pull you're carrying: a crush, a craving, the urge to send a message at midnight. Don't push it away, and don't follow it; let it sit beside you, the way you'd sit beside a friend who's upset. On each breath out, feel the space between the feeling and the act, and notice you're still the one choosing.
Nikah. Marriage, the contract that makes a home of two people; the place the tradition gives to closeness, and the reason for getting to know someone.
Your line: a feeling isn't a sin. What you do with it is the choice. That's day one hundred forty-four.

screen: `DAY 144 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE NAME ON THE MEAT.`

howItsDone: Many Muslim families and communities encourage getting to know a possible spouse with marriage in mind, through introductions, family involvement, public meetings or marriage-focused apps, and keep physical closeness for marriage; where the lines fall varies by family and teacher.

what it means: nikah — closeness belongs in marriage, getting to know someone for marriage is encouraged, and a feeling isn't a sin.
what a scholar hears: 17:32, la taqrabu z-zina (don't come near); khalwa and Tirmidhi 2165; looking before proposing (Tirmidhi 1087); Bukhari 5269 on what the soul whispers; Ibn Majah 1847.

notes: Rewritten 2026-10-06 from the five-year map; confirm with the Keeper.

NEW lesson from the map's #2 change ('is it haram to date?', the most-asked teen question in the research and absent before: AUDIENCE_RESEARCH_ISLAM.md Top 20 #12, Quora #16–17). It follows day 143 ('most things are allowed'), the natural next question. It replaces 'Good and wholesome' (tayyib, 2:168 and 'Allah is good and accepts only what is good', Muslim 1015); tayyib is still glossed in day 156's day-in-the-life ('something halal and good'), and the good-word, good-tree verse is day 446. Muslim 1015 is no longer taught in year 1.

Sensitive (teen audience): the lesson states the near-universal agreement (no sex outside nikah; caution about seclusion), describes 'dating' in its movie sense as outside the lines for most scholars, and presents the ways communities meet ('with intention', chaperones, introductions, apps) as places families differ, without endorsing a model. It never says dating is fine. It deliberately leaves out interfaith marriage and LGBTQ questions (out of scope per the map).
Pickthall 17:32 quoted from memory; please check.
